1.2.PAIN RELIEF DURING LABOR:

Non – pharmacological strategies:

•Breathing exercises - Support women’s
•Shower or bath choice.
•Massage - Reduce pain during latent 1st stage.

Psychological:

•Lamaze (most popular)
•Bradley
•Leboyer

 

 

•Aromatherapy - Don’t offer for pain relief.
•Yoga - If women want, then
•Acupressure respect her wishes.

TENS – Support her choices.

 

(Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation).

•Acupuncture - Don’t offer
•Acupressure - Support her choice if
•Hypnosis if she requests.

 

•Playing music – support
•Water birth – offer
-Keep baths and birthing pools clean in collaboration with microbiology department.
-Keep temp up to 37.50C not more than that.
-Check temp 1 hourly.
-Avoid water birth within 2 hours of opioids.
•Birthing Ball
-Reduce pain 30 – 40%

Shorten 1st stage

-Less need of C/S and epidural analgesia

Sterile water Injection:

•Consider for pain relief in women with back pain.
•Midwife can inject who is trained
•It can provide pain relief after 10min of injection up to 3 hours, but there is initial stinging sensation.
•Method
-4 different injection points.
-Around Rhombus Michalis
-0.1ml intracutaneous or
-0.5ml subcutaneous at each injection point.

Inhalational Analgesia:

•Should be available in all birth settings
•50:50 Mixture of oxygen and nitrous oxide.
•Feeling of nausea and light headedness.

Pharmacological Analgesia:

⇨Pethidine, Diamorphine and other opioids:
-Pethidine 150mg I/M
-Diamorphine 7.5mg I/M - All birth
-Other opioids setting.
⇨Meperidine
-10-25mg I/V
-25-50mg I/M
⇨Fentanyl
-25-100mcg/h
•Side effect:
-Drowsiness
-Nausea Mother
-Vomiting
-Drowsiness
-Difficult feeding Baby readily
-Short term crosses the

respiratory placenta.

problems

•Use I/M or I/V antiemetic’s.
•Avoid water birth for 2 hours.
⇨I/V remifentanil PCA
•Patient control analgesia.
•Consultant let unit/obstetric unit risk of respiratory depression requiring anesthetist input.
•40mg per bolus
•2 min lock out period
•Less chance of need for epidural
•Less chance of forceps or ventouse delivery
•More chance of spontaneous birth
•More chance of supplemental oxygen
•One to one midwifery support
•CCTG if risk factors present
•Continuous monitoring of Breathing and pulse oximetry.

Others:

•Promethazine – 25 - 50mg I/M.
•Hydroxyzine – 50 - 100mg I/M.
⇨Regional Analgesia:

i. Nerve Block – Pudendal Nerve Block (for 2nd stage of labour)

ii. Epidural – Opioids/Local Anesthetics

iii. Spinal:

i.Spinal Opioids Alone
ii.Local Anaesthetic
iii.Local Anaesthetic – Opioids Mixture.

iv. Combine Spinal Epidural

Only obstetric unit

•More effective pain relief
•Sometimes not fully effective, need to be adjusted
•No long-term backache
•No prolonged 1st stage.
•No ed chance of C/S
• prolonged 2nd stage
• Ed chance of forceps or ventouse delivery

•Reduced mobility
• ed chance of headache

Care and observation with regional analgesia:

•I/V line
•Pre – loading and maintenance fluids not required with low dose epidural or combined spinal – epidural
•Monitor B.P every 5 min for 15 min after loading dose and maintenance doses (10ml or above)
• Talk to anesthetist if not pain free after 30min of dose
•Assess sensory block level 1 hourly.
•Assess motor block 1 hourly by asking to do straight leg raise. If she is unable to raise leg, ask anesthetist to review.
•Adapt position whatever she likes except lying flat on her back.
•Mobilize if can
•Delayed pushing for 1 hours in multi and 1 hour in primigravida after full dilatation unless she has an urge to actively push. After this time encourage woman to actively push during contraction.
•No oxytocin routinely
•cCTG for 30min after loading dose as well as after each bolus of 10ml or above.
•Continue regional analgesia until completion of 3rd stage of labor or perineal tear repair.

Establishing and Maintaining Regional Analgesia:

•Use either epidural or combined spinal – epidural analgesia for establishing regional analgesia in labour
•If rapid analgesia is needed use CSE
•Establish CSE with bupivacaine and fentanyl
•Establish epidural analgesia with a low concentration local anesthetic and fentanyl solution – administer test dose initially to ensure that in-advertent intrathecal or intra vascular placement of epidural catheter has not occurred.
•Maintenance dose should be low concentration solution. 0.0625% to 0.125%
•Bupivacaine combined with 2-3 micrograms per ml fentanyl.
•Bupivacaine or equivalent can be used as local anesthetic component of solution.
•Patient controlled epidural analgesia can be used by trained healthcare professional for maintenance.
•Don’t use high concentration solution of local anesthetic 0.25% or above routinely either for establishment or maintenance.

PROM:

•Advice women to call midwife immediately on phone.
•Immediate review of a women if risk factor present.

Risk factors:

•Meconium-stained liquor
•Vaginal bleeding
•RFM
•Continuous abdominal pain
•Unpleasant smelling liquor or change in smell of vaginal discharge.
•Feeling unwell
•GBS carriage or infection in current or previous pregnancy, where there is plan of IP Antibiotic prophylaxis.
•Abnormal fetal lie
•FGR
•Low lying placenta.

Immediate review of women with PROM

•Above risk factor present
•Women have any concern
•Women want IOL
•Something changed.

Home review by Midwife:

•If no risk factor
•Women want to wait for spontaneous onset of labour
⇨Don’t offer speculum examination if it is certain that membranes have ruptured.
⇨Offer speculum examination if diagnosis is not clear
⇨Don’t offer digital examination in the absence of contractions.
⇨60% women with PROM go into labour in 24 hours
⇨Neonatal risk with PROM 1% rather 0.5% with intact membranes.
⇨Discuss benefits and risks of expectant management vs IOL
⇨If women choses expectant management
•No need of vaginal swab and CRP
•Temp recording 4 hourly during walking hour and report immediately if change happens.
•Any change in color and smell of vaginal discharge do report immediately
•Can take shower or bath
•Avoid sexual intercourse – risk of infection.
•FM and FHR @ initial visit and then every 24 hours till in labor. Advice women to report immediately if there is RFM.
•If labour is not started after 24 hours of PROM, advice women to give birth in alongside midwifery unit or obstetric unit because there is risk of neonatal complication and maternal infection. She is also advised to stay at least for 12 hours after birth.
•If women are GBS positive at any stage of this pregnancy or had baby with GBS infection, offer immediate birth along with IPA prophylaxis.
